text:
Marathon Petroleum's stock has fallen sharply over the past week—dropping roughly 11% from November 13 to today—despite today's move being nearly flat. The main driver appears to be the collapse in crude oil prices: US oil fell from above $100 a barrel earlier this month to $89.53 today, a drop of roughly 10%. Refiners like Marathon make money on the spread between the crude they buy and the refined products (gasoline, diesel) they sell; when crude prices fall faster than product prices follow, that margin compresses, hurting profitability.

The broader concern is that geopolitical risk—which had been supporting oil prices—is fading. Reports of Iran-backed attacks on Saudi Arabia and Bahrain briefly kept energy markets elevated, but those concerns don't appear to have stuck. With refineries already running at a healthy 95.7% capacity and storage levels stable, there's no supply-side tightness to prop up prices either, leaving crude vulnerable to demand concerns or shifts in investor positioning.
